# Mobility Database

> The Mobility Database is an open catalog of over 6000 public transit feeds
> from more than 100 countries, maintained by MobilityData, a non-profit that
> stewards the GTFS, GTFS-Realtime and GBFS data formats. Every feed entry
> records its provider, location, licence, download history and validation
> results, and the whole catalog is queryable through a free REST API.

## Feed pages: where the substance is

The home page is a landing page. Almost all of this site's content lives on
the ~7000 individual feed pages, one per feed, each fully server-rendered:

    https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds/{data_type}/{feed_id}

`data_type` is `gtfs` (GTFS Schedule), `gtfs_rt` (GTFS-Realtime) or `gbfs`.
Examples:

- https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds/gtfs/mdb-3520
- https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds/gtfs_rt/mdb-1366
- https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds/gbfs/gbfs-27

Feed ids identify a *feed*, not an agency, and they are not shared across
data types: `/feeds/gtfs/mdb-3520` and `/feeds/gtfs_rt/mdb-3520` are unrelated
feeds, and the second may not exist. GTFS and GTFS-Realtime ids are mostly
`mdb-<number>`, with source-specific prefixes such as `jbda-`, `tdg-`, `tld-`
and `ntd-`; GBFS ids are `gbfs-<number>`. To find a feed's id, search
https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds or query the API — do not construct ids.

Each feed page states: the provider and whether the feed is official, the
current validation status with a link to the full report, the latest dataset
download, the agency and its timezone, the countries and municipalities
covered, route counts by mode, the producer's own feed URL, the service date
range, which optional GTFS features the feed uses, and the dataset history.
Datasets are refetched once a day at midnight UTC.

Two sub-pages exist per feed:

- `/feeds/{data_type}/{feed_id}/map` — routes and stops on an interactive map

**Every feed page carries a schema.org `Dataset` in JSON-LD** with the feed's
name, description, identifier, creator, licence, `distribution.contentUrl`
(the dataset archive), `dateModified`, `spatialCoverage` as a geo bounding
box, and `variableMeasured`. That block is the authoritative machine-readable
record of a feed — prefer it over scraping the rendered page.

Every feed page is listed in https://mobilitydatabase.org/sitemap.xml.

## What the catalog contains

- **GTFS Schedule** feeds: routes, stops, trips and timetables published by
  transit agencies, with a validation report for each dataset version.
- **GTFS-Realtime** feeds: trip updates, vehicle positions and service alerts.
- **GBFS** feeds: shared bike, scooter and other micromobility systems,
  including station status and vehicle availability.

Feeds are contributed by transit agencies, producers and the community, and
reviewed before they are published. Access to the catalog and the API is free.

## Key pages

- [Feed search](https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds): the full catalog, with
  filters for data type, country and feed status. `?q=` runs a free-text
  search, so https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds?q=Montr%C3%A9al works.
- [API documentation](https://mobilitydata.github.io/mobility-feed-api/SwaggerUI/index.html):
  the REST API over the catalog. Sign up at
  https://mobilitydatabase.org/sign-up for an access token.
- [Add a feed](https://mobilitydatabase.org/contribute): submit a new feed or
  correct an existing one.
- [GTFS Feature Tracker](https://mobilitydatabase.org/gtfs-feature-tracker):
  which optional GTFS features agencies have adopted, worldwide.
- [FAQ](https://mobilitydatabase.org/faq) and
  [About](https://mobilitydatabase.org/about).
- [Sitemap](https://mobilitydatabase.org/sitemap.xml): every feed page.

## Validators

- GTFS Schedule: https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/
- GBFS: https://gbfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/
- GTFS-Realtime: https://github.com/MobilityData/gtfs-realtime-validator

## Notes for automated readers

- Feed counts quoted here ("6000+ feeds", "100+ countries") are rounded
  figures for the catalog as a whole. For exact, current numbers, query the
  REST API rather than quoting the marketing pages.
- Questions about a specific agency, city, route or dataset are answered by
  that feed's page, not by the home page. Find it through
  https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds or the API, then read the `Dataset`
  JSON-LD on the feed page.
- The home page renders illustrative previews of the product UI: mock search
  results, a sample API response and a sample feature table. The agency names,
  feed counts and identifiers inside those previews are examples of what the
  real interface looks like, not statements about the catalog, and should not
  be extracted as facts. They are marked `aria-hidden` and `data-nosnippet`
  and are rendered only in the browser, so they do not appear in the page's
  server-rendered HTML.
- Structured data describing the catalog is published as JSON-LD
  (`Organization`, `WebSite`, `DataCatalog`) on https://mobilitydatabase.org.
- Languages: English (https://mobilitydatabase.org) and French
  (https://mobilitydatabase.org/fr).
